headline: Sequencing growth continues; profit dips on tough GRAIL comp
summary_short: Illumina's Q2 2026 revenue rose 9.4% y/y (+6.2% q/q) to $1,159M on NovaSeq X consumables/instrument demand and the SomaLogic acquisition, while net income fell 11.9% y/y to $207M and diluted EPS fell to $1.35 as a large prior-year GRAIL investment gain did not repeat.
summary_long: Revenue rose 9.4% y/y to $1,159M on NovaSeq X consumables/instrument demand and the SomaLogic acquisition, partly offset by a $7M China revenue headwind tied to the unreliable-entities-list inclusion. Gross margin rose to 66.4% y/y, but the comparison is inflated by a $23M Q2 2025 intangible impairment; excluding it, margin fell on mix shift toward lower-margin instruments, higher memory/freight costs, and SomaLogic dilution. Net income fell 11.9% y/y to $207M and diluted EPS to $1.35 because Q2 2025 included a large GRAIL investment gain that did not repeat. Cash fell to $1,040M (-4.5% q/q) after $417M paid for SomaLogic and $370M of buybacks. No explicit FY2026 guidance range was given in this filing.

drivers.explanation: Management reiterated 2024-set goals of returning to revenue growth and improving margins by 2027, citing NovaSeq X-driven demand alongside continuing tariff, China-market, and Middle-East-conflict cost headwinds.

Consumables grew on NovaSeq X installed-base demand; instruments grew on higher NovaSeq X and MiSeq i100 shipments; service revenue grew on the SomaLogic acquisition and licensing/informatics growth, partly offset by a $7M China revenue drop tied to the unreliable-entities-list inclusion.

The y/y increase is largely a base-effect from a $23M intangible impairment taken in Q2 2025; excluding that one-off, margin actually fell on mix shift toward lower-margin instruments, higher memory and freight costs, and SomaLogic dilution, partly offset by lower tariff costs.
Gross profit rose $75M against a $44M rise in operating expense, netting a $31M increase in Q2 operating income.

Other income (expense) swung lower because Q2 2025 included a comparatively larger gain on Illumina's retained GRAIL investment than Q2 2026, pulling pretax income down 15% y/y despite higher operating income.
Diluted EPS fell 9.4% y/y, a smaller decline than net income's 11.9% drop, because weighted diluted shares fell 2.5% y/y on continued share repurchases.

Q2 2026 equity rose $162M q/q: $207M net income plus $72M share-based compensation and a $7M hedge gain, partly offset by $124M of net share issuance/repurchase activity, per the equity roll-forward table.
Weighted diluted shares fell on continued repurchases under the 2024/2026 $1.5B buyback programs (942 thousand shares bought in the open market in Q2 2026), outpacing dilution from equity awards.
